column1: # Line-count tolerance for a ported file, over and above the 5% the rule allows every
# file.  The line count is a crude drift signal - the per-function token check is the real
# guard - so a file whose ledger records a *structural* expansion of C's text (a form Rust
# cannot spell in the same number of physical lines) declares its tolerance here with the
# reason, instead of losing the readability of the port to fit 5%.  One
# `<stem>\t<tolerance>\t<reason>\t<basis>` per line; the check uses max(0.05, tolerance).
# `<basis>` is `total` (the default, and what every older row means) or `live`:
#   total - the baseline is the reference file's whole line count.  Right for a port that
#           carries *more* text than C, including the P-51 dead arms kept as
#   live  - the baseline is the C text this configuration actually compiles
#           (`c_live_lines`: the same branch evaluator the declarations use).  For a file
#           whose dead region is *recorded in its ledger instead of transcribed*
#           total-line baseline would demand a ~0.99 tolerance that silences the check
#           entirely; against the live baseline the check still points at the text the port
